newsitem.title: USA: Texaco possible split causes little reaction.
newsitem.headline: Texaco possible split causes little reaction.

text.p: The announcement of a possible stock split from a U.S. oil major, Texaco Inc, produced little immediate reaction on Wall Street and the shares slid 1/2 to 98-3/8 by 1500 EST/2000 GMT.

"I cannot really see what this accomplishes on a corporate level. There is clearly a desire among these companies to broaden their investor base beyond the institutions and attract some of the money flowing into mutual funds," said Paul Ting, who heads oil company research at Salomon Brothers in New York.
Mobil Corp and refiner Tosco Corp announced definite share splits earlier this year.

Texaco said on Monday that it would seek shareholder approval to double the number of its common shares and reduce the stock price from $6.25 face value to $3.125, saying instead that the move would increase flexibility for "acquisitions, financings, stock splits, stock dividends and other corporate purposes." It stopped short of saying it was actually planning a stock split.
Since Mobil announced a two-for-one split at the end of January, its shares have fallen from 131-1/4 to 125, while Tosco is off from 29-1/2 to 28 since its announcement on February 12.
"These shares are much more sensitive to the price outlook for crude, which has deteriorated," said Salomon's Ting.

Since the start of 1997, oil company shares have fallen one percent, compared with a seven percent rise in the S&P 500 index, as the price for the benchmark West Texas Intermediate crude blend has fallen from a January peak of $26.00 per barrel to close to $20.00.
